literal: Without yet troubling our axes and halberds, they have already submitted to Heaven's execution; descendants slaughter one another, kin and clans split in two; the false commanders at Kuan and Lo all harbor secret intent to submit inward, and the remnant people north of the Ho turn their loyalty and beg to serve with effect.
idiomatic: Without our having yet lifted axe or halberd, Heaven's judgment has already fallen on them; their sons and grandsons slaughter one another, and kin and allies divide against each other; the puppet leaders at Kuan and Lo all secretly wish to surrender, and the people left north of the Ho fix their hearts on us and plead to be put to use.

literal: To rescue the drowning and sweep away filth—now is the moment.
idiomatic: To save the drowning and cleanse away corruption—now is the time.

literal: Let orders be sent to the two bureaus of the Rapid Cavalry General and the Minister of Works, that each take charge of what he commands and coordinate east and west.
idiomatic: Orders should go to the Rapid Cavalry General and the Minister of Works, that each division under their command respond in concert east and west.

literal: Those who submit in allegiance and establish merit shall be rewarded according to their labor.
idiomatic: Those who come over in good faith and achieve merit shall be rewarded in proportion to their service.

literal: " That month, the capital metropolis suffered rain and flooding.
idiomatic: That month the capital region was afflicted by rain and flood.

literal: On the sixth month, day chiyu, envoys of the ministry were dispatched to tour the districts, granting firewood and grain and providing boats.
idiomatic: On chiyu day in the sixth month, ministry envoys were sent on circuit through the districts, distributing firewood and grain and supplying boats.

literal: General Who Pacifies the Army Xiao Sihua led troops on a northern campaign.
idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the Army, led an army north.

literal: Liu Yu, Attendant Clerk on the Staff of the General Who Campaigns North, was made Governor of Yi Province.
idiomatic: Liu Yu, attendant clerk on the staff of the General Who Campaigns North, was appointed Governor of Yi Province.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jenchen day, Prince of Ju-yin Hun was redesignated Prince of Wu-ch'ang, and Prince of Huai-yang Yu was redesignated Prince of Hsiang-tung.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jenchen day, Prince of Ju-yin Hun was redesignated Prince of Wu-ch'ang, and Prince of Huai-yang Yu was redesignated Prince of Hsiang-tung.

literal: On the tingyu day, the posts of Supervisor of the Grand Granary, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Assistant in the Court of Justice were abolished.
idiomatic: On the tingyu day, the offices of Supervisor of the Grand Granary, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Assistant in the Court of Justice were abolished.

literal: On the tingmao day of the eighth month, Xiao Sihua attacked Ch'üeh-p'o but could not capture it and withdrew.
idiomatic: On tingmao day in the eighth month, Xiao Sihua attacked Ch'üeh-p'o, failed to take it, and withdrew.

literal: On the tinghai day of the ninth month, Shih-yin of the Tuyuhun, General Who Pacifies the West, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ch'in and Ho provinces.
idiomatic: On tinghai day in the ninth month, Shih-yin of the Tuyuhun, General Who Pacifies the West, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Ch'in and Ho provinces.

literal: On the chichou day, Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was additionally made Governor of Chi Province; his governorship of Yen Province remained as before.
idiomatic: On the chichou day, Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was additionally appointed Governor of Chi Province while retaining Yen Province.

literal: On the kueihai day of the tenth month of winter, Lu Shuang, Inspector of Ssu Province, attacked Hu-lao but could not capture it and withdrew.
idiomatic: On kueihai day in the tenth month of winter, Lu Shuang, Inspector of Ssu Province, attacked Hu-lao, failed to take it, and withdrew.

literal: On the jenyin day of the eleventh month, Shao, Prince of Lu-ling and Governor of Yang Province, died.
idiomatic: On jen-yin day in the eleventh month, Shao, Prince of Lu-ling and Governor of Yang Province, died.

literal: On the hsinwei day of the twelfth month, Yigong, Prince of Chiang-hsia, Rapid Cavalry General and Governor of Southern Yen Province, was made Grand General and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, with Recorder of the Masters of Writing as before.
idiomatic: On hsin-wei day in the twelfth month, Yigong, Prince of Chiang-hsia, Rapid Cavalry General and Governor of Southern Yen Province, was appointed Grand General and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, retaining his post as Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: In the first month of spring of the thirtieth year, on the wuyin day, Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, Minister of Works and Governor of Ching Province, was made Minister over the Masses, General of the Central Army, and Governor of Yang Province.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the thirtieth year, on the wu-yin day, Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, Minister of Works and Governor of Ching Province, became Minister over the Masses, General of the Central Army, and Governor of Yang Province.

literal: Southern Yen Province was merged into Southern Hsü Province.
idiomatic: Southern Yen Province was merged into Southern Hsü Province.

literal: On the kengch'en day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Guards, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Province.
idiomatic: On the keng-ch'en day, Liu Tsun-k'ao, General of the Guards, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Province.

literal: On the jenwu day, Chun, Prince of Shih-hsing, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General of the Guard and Governor of Ching Province.
idiomatic: On jen-wu day, Chun, Prince of Shih-hsing, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was appointed General of the Guard and Governor of Ching Province.

literal: On the wutzu day, Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, commanded the armies in a campaign against the Hsi-yang barbarians.
idiomatic: On wu-tzu day, Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, took command of the armies to campaign against the Hsi-yang barbarians.

literal: On the kueissu day, Shuo, Prince of Nan-p'ing and Inspector of Yu Province, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and General of the Guards.
idiomatic: On kuei-ssu day, Shuo, Prince of Nan-p'ing and Inspector of Yu Province, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and General of the Guards.

literal: Ch'ing and Hsü provinces suffered famine; on the jentzu day of the second month, the Transport Bureau was dispatched to grant relief.
idiomatic: Ch'ing and Hsü provinces suffered famine; on jen-tzu day in the second month, the Transport Bureau was sent to provide relief.

literal: On the chia-tzu day, the Emperor died in the Han-chang Palace.
idiomatic: On chia-tzu day, the Emperor died in the Han-chang Palace.

literal: He was forty-seven years old.
idiomatic: He was forty-seven years old.

literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Ching; his temple name was Chung-tsung.
idiomatic: His posthumous title was Emperor Ching; his temple name was Chung-tsung.

literal: On the kueissu day of the third month, he was buried at the Ch'ang-ning Mausoleum.
idiomatic: On kuei-ssu day in the third month, he was buried at the Ch'ang-ning Mausoleum.

literal: When Shih-tsu ascended the throne, he retroactively changed the posthumous title and temple name.
idiomatic: When Shih-tsu came to the throne, he altered the posthumous title and temple name retroactively.

literal: The historian says: In his youth the Grand Ancestor was exceptionally gifted; though he lacked the strict tutelage of a guardian and tutor, Heaven bestowed upon him a harmonious and keen nature, and he was himself endowed with the virtue of a ruler of men.
idiomatic: The historian writes: In youth the Grand Ancestor was singularly gifted; though he had no stern guardian or tutor, Heaven granted him a harmonious, quick mind, and he was born with the virtue of a true sovereign.

literal: When he took the throne facing south, his years in power were long; the framework of government was fully established, statutes and prohibitions were clear and close, punishments had fixed measures, and ranks and titles were never bestowed without warrant.
idiomatic: Once enthroned, he ruled for many years; the pillars of government stood complete, laws and prohibitions were lucid and strict, penalties followed fixed standards, and ennoblement was never careless.

literal: Thus within was purity and without was peace; the four seas were tranquil.
idiomatic: Thus within the realm was order and without was calm; all under Heaven was still.

literal: Formerly the Eastern Han often spoke of the precedents of Chien-wu and Yung-p'ing; after that age as well, men regularly cited the Yüan-chia reign as their model—truly this was greatness.
idiomatic: In the Eastern Han men often invoked the precedents of Chien-wu and Yung-p'ing; in later times too the Yüan-chia era was held up as the standard—such was its greatness.

literal: Yet in appointing generals and dispatching commanders he went against the proper division of frontier authority; his talent fell short of Emperor Kuang-wu's, yet he remotely controlled military strategy—so that when it came to the day of battle, none failed to look upward and obey the final order from court.
idiomatic: Yet in appointing generals and sending out commanders he violated the proper division of frontier authority; his gifts were no match for Emperor Kuang-wu's, yet he directed strategy from afar—so that on the day of battle every move awaited the court's final word.

literal: Though armies were shattered and hosts lost, and his generals were no Han Hsin or Pai Ch'i, the prolongation of enemy raids and grief at the borders sprang chiefly from this cause.
idiomatic: Though campaigns ended in rout and commanders were no Han Hsin or Pai Ch'i, the lingering raids and border calamity owed chiefly to this.

literal: When at last word leaked beside the pillow and difficulty entangled him with a merchant of Shang, though disaster arose beyond foresight, there was reason for it to happen thus.
idiomatic: When words at last leaked from the pillow and trouble bound him to a peddler of Shang, though the catastrophe was unlooked-for, it had its causes.

literal: Alas, how lamentable!
idiomatic: Alas, how lamentable!

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Textual collation notes

literal: When the imperial carriage reached the capital city. Sun Ao's Song Shu textual commentary says: "It should read the capital metropolis.
idiomatic: "When the imperial carriage reached the capital city." Sun Ao's Song Shu textual commentary says: "It should read the capital metropolis.

literal: The capital city would then mean Ching-k'ou.
idiomatic: Capital city would mean Ching-k'ou.

literal: " According to the Comprehensive Mirror, it reads Chien-k'ang.
idiomatic: " According to the Comprehensive Mirror, the text reads Chien-k'ang.

literal: In the Sung shu, capital city often refers to the city of Ching-k'ou; here it refers to Chien-k'ang.
idiomatic: In the Book of Song, capital city often means Ching-k'ou; here it means Chien-k'ang.

literal: On hsin-wei the imperial carriage sacrificed at the southern suburb. All editions omit the two characters hsin-wei; they are supplied according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, the Veritable Record of Chien-k'ang, and the Comprehensive Mirror.
idiomatic: On hsin-wei the imperial carriage sacrificed at the southern suburb. All editions omit hsin-wei; the date is restored from the History of the Southern Dynasties, the Veritable Record of Chien-k'ang, and the Comprehensive Mirror.

literal: Administrator of Chien-an P'an Sheng was guilty of a crime and was executed. "P'an Sheng": all editions read "P'an Ch'eng"; changed according to the Annals of the Young Emperor and the biography of Hsü Hsien-chih.
idiomatic: P'an Sheng, Administrator of Chien-an, was found guilty and executed. "P'an Sheng": all editions read "P'an Ch'eng"; corrected from the Annals of the Young Emperor and the biography of Hsü Hsien-chih.

literal: Yi-mao. All editions read i-mao; changed according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: Yi-mao. All editions read i-mao; emended according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-yu; the nineteenth day was yi-mao—there was no i-mao.
idiomatic: That month's new moon fell on ting-yu; the nineteenth day was yi-mao—there was no i-mao.

literal: Concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province. All editions omit the character nan; according to the biography of the Prince of P'eng-ch'eng Yikang, the Veritable Record of Chien-k'ang, and the Comprehensive Mirror, all read Governor of Southern Hsü Province—now supplied.
idiomatic: Concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province. All editions drop nan; the biography of Prince of P'eng-ch'eng Yikang, the Veritable Record of Chien-k'ang, and the Comprehensive Mirror all have Southern Hsü—restored here.

literal: Former General Who Campaigns the Barbarians Staff Officer Yin Ch'ung was made Inspector of Ssu Province. All editions omit the character Yin; according to the biography of the Northern Barbarians, at this time Yin Ch'ung was Inspector of Ssu Province, as does the Comprehensive Mirror.
idiomatic: Former staff officer on the General Who Campaigns the Barbarians Yin Ch'ung was made Inspector of Ssu Province. All editions omit Yin; the Northern Barbarians biography and the Comprehensive Mirror both have Yin Ch'ung as inspector at this time.

literal: Now supplied.
idiomatic: Restored accordingly.

literal: Grand General Who Campaigns South Tan Tao-chi defeated the Northern Barbarians at Tung-p'ing Shou-chang. All editions omit the character p'ing.
idiomatic: Tan Tao-chi, Grand General Who Campaigns South, defeated the Northern Barbarians at Tung-p'ing Shou-chang. All editions omit p'ing.

literal: Supplied according to the biography of Tan Tao-chi.
idiomatic: Supplied from the biography of Tan Tao-chi.

literal: Hung I-hsuan's Various Histories Textual Notes says: "According to the biography of Tan Tao-chi it reads Tung-p'ing Shou-chang; here the character p'ing is missing below tung."
idiomatic: Hung I-hsuan's Various Histories Textual Notes says: "The biography of Tan Tao-chi reads Tung-p'ing Shou-chang; here p'ing is missing after tung."

literal: If one does not deeply preserve the root of affairs. All editions omit the character kou; supplied according to Yuan Kuei 198.
idiomatic: "If one does not deeply preserve the root of affairs." All editions omit kou; supplied from Yuan Kuei 198.

literal: Mu-yen of the Tuyuhun was made General Who Pacifies the East. "Mu-yen": the Tuyuhun biography in this book reads "Mu-yen."
idiomatic: Mu-yen of the Tuyuhun was made General Who Pacifies the East. "Mu-yen": the Tuyuhun biography in this book reads "Mu-yen."

literal: The Wei shu reads "Mu Li-yen."
idiomatic: The Book of Wei reads "Mu Li-yen."

literal: Hui-fa of the Tuyuhun was made General Who Garrisons the Army. All editions omit the character ku; supplied according to the usage elsewhere in the text.
idiomatic: Hui-fa of the Tuyuhun was made General Who Garrisons the Army. All editions omit ku in Tuyuhun; restored by parallel passages.

literal: "Hui-fa": the Wei shu reads "Wei-tai."
idiomatic: "Hui-fa": the Book of Wei reads "Wei-tai."

literal: On jen-shen the King of Ho-nan and the King of Ho-hsi of the Ho-nan state sent envoys presenting local products. "King of Ho-hsi": all editions read "King of Hsi-ho"; changed according to the Annals of the Young Emperor for the first year of Ching-p'ing and the biography of the Great Chü-ch'ü Meng-sun.
idiomatic: On jen-shen the King of Ho-nan and the King of Ho-hsi of the Ho-nan state sent envoys bearing tribute. "King of Ho-hsi": all editions read "King of Hsi-ho"; corrected from the Young Emperor annals for Ching-p'ing year 1 and the biography of Meng-sun of the Great Chü-ch'ü.

literal: The outlaw Ma Ta-hsüan and his band of several hundred men raided T'ai-shan. The Three Dynasties edition reads "T'ai-shan"; the Hung-chih, Northern Directorate, Mao, Hall, and Bureau editions read "Ch'in-liang."
idiomatic: The outlaw Ma Ta-hsüan and his band of several hundred raided T'ai-shan. The Three Dynasties edition reads T'ai-shan; the Hung-chih, Northern Directorate, Mao, Hall, and Bureau editions read Ch'in-liang.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, day i-yu. According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-hai—there was no i-yu.
idiomatic: Fourth month of summer, i-yu day. That month's new moon was ting-hai—there was no i-yu.

literal: The twenty-third day was chi-yu; "i-yu" is probably a corruption for "chi-yu."
idiomatic: The twenty-third day was chi-yu; i-yu is probably a scribal error for chi-yu.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, hsin-yu. "Hsin-yu": all editions read "i-yu"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: Seventh month of autumn, hsin-yu. "Hsin-yu": all editions read i-yu; emended from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on keng-hsu; the sixth day was hsin-yu—there was no "i-yu."
idiomatic: That month's new moon was keng-hsu; the sixth day was hsin-yu—there was no i-yu.

literal: In Yi Province the three commanderies of Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi were established. All editions read "In Yi Province the three commanderies of Southern Chin-shou, Hsin-pa, and Pa-hsi were established."
idiomatic: In Yi Province the three commanderies Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi were established. All editions read "Southern Chin-shou, Hsin-pa, and Pa-hsi."

literal: Sun Ao's Song Shu textual commentary says: "According to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, these are the three commanderies of Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi."
idiomatic: Sun Ao's Song Shu textual commentary says: "According to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, these are Southern Chin-shou, Southern Hsin-pa, and Northern Pa-hsi."

literal: According to Sun's view this is correct; now emended.
idiomatic: Sun's reading is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

literal: Again, in the entry above it says "jen-shen," and below it says "i-hai."
idiomatic: The line above reads jen-shen and the line below i-hai.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ping-hsu—there was neither jen-shen nor i-hai.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was ping-hsu—neither jen-shen nor i-hai occurred.

literal: Colonel of Footsoldiers Liu Chen-tao was made Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces. "Liu Chen-tao": all editions read "Liu Tao-chen."
idiomatic: Liu Chen-tao, Colonel of Footsoldiers, was made Governor of Liang and Southern Ch'in provinces. "Liu Chen-tao": all editions read "Liu Tao-chen."

literal: Chang Sen-k'ai's collation note says: "It should read Liu Chen-tao, as in the biography of Liu Huai-su; in the eighteenth year below it also reads Liu Chen-tao.
idiomatic: Chang Sen-k'ai's collation note says: "It should be Liu Chen-tao, as in the biography of Liu Huai-su; the eighteenth year below also has Liu Chen-tao.

literal: " According to Chang's view this is correct; now corrected.
idiomatic: " Chang's view is accepted; the text is corrected.

literal: The King of Ho-nan and the King of Ho-hsi of the Ho-nan state, and the state of Ho-lo-tan, all sent envoys presenting local products. "King of Ho-hsi": all editions read "King of Hsi-ho"; changed according to the Annals of the Young Emperor and the biography of the Great Chü-ch'ü Meng-sun.
idiomatic: The kings of Ho-nan and Ho-hsi of the Ho-nan state and the state of Ho-lo-tan all sent envoys bearing tribute. "King of Ho-hsi": all editions read "King of Hsi-ho"; corrected from the Young Emperor annals and the biography of Meng-sun of the Great Chü-ch'ü.

literal: The King of Yen Hung sent envoys presenting local products. "Hung": all editions read "Nien"; changed according to the annals section of the Chin shu.
idiomatic: King Hung of Yen sent envoys bearing tribute. "Hung": all editions read "Nien"; corrected from the annals in the Book of Chin.

literal: Where this year there are districts without harvest. "Year": all editions read "half"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 489.
idiomatic: "Where this year there are districts without harvest." "Year": all editions read "half"; emended from Yuan Kuei 489.

literal: Wang Ch'iu, Grandee of Splendid Virtue, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing. "Wang Ch'iu": all editions read "Wang Lin"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
idiomatic: Wang Ch'iu, Grandee of Splendid Virtue, was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing. "Wang Ch'iu": all editions read "Wang Lin"; corrected from the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.

literal: Hung I-hsuan's Various Histories Textual Notes says: "Wang Ch'iu written as Wang Lin is a scribal corruption."
idiomatic: Hung I-hsuan's Various Histories Textual Notes says: "Wang Ch'iu written as Wang Lin is a copyist's error."

literal: In the fifth month of summer, jen-wu. "Jen-wu": all editions read "jen-shen."
idiomatic: Fifth month of summer, jen-wu. "Jen-wu": all editions read jen-shen.

literal: The Bureau edition reads "jen-wu."
idiomatic: The Bureau edition reads jen-wu.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on jen-wu—there was no jen-shen.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was jen-wu—there was no jen-shen.

literal: Now follow the Bureau edition.
idiomatic: The Bureau reading is adopted.

literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Ch'iu died. "Ch'iu": all editions read "Lin"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
idiomatic: Wang Ch'iu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, died. "Ch'iu": all editions read "Lin"; corrected from the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.

literal: That month. All editions read "twelfth month."
idiomatic: That month. All editions read twelfth month.

literal: According to the text above, the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth months have already appeared—it cannot again have a twelfth month.
idiomatic: The tenth, eleventh, and twelfth months already appear above—a second twelfth month is impossible.

literal: Now changed to read "that month."
idiomatic: The text is changed to "that month."

literal: In a flourishing age of sage rule. "Sage": all editions read "ancestor"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 194.
idiomatic: "In a flourishing age of sage rule." "Sage": all editions read "ancestor"; emended from Yuan Kuei 194.

literal: For the first time performing the yü sacrifice. "Yü": all editions read "first"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 207.
idiomatic: "For the first time performing the yü sacrifice." "Yü": all editions read "first"; emended from Yuan Kuei 207.

literal: Keng-shen. All editions agree.
idiomatic: Keng-shen. All editions agree.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on jen-shen; the third day was chia-hsu—that month had no keng-shen.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was jen-shen; the third day was chia-hsu—there was no keng-shen in that month.

literal: Below there is chia-shen, which is the thirteenth day.
idiomatic: Below comes chia-shen, the thirteenth day.

literal: Between chia-hsu and chia-shen there is keng-ch'en.
idiomatic: Between chia-hsu and chia-shen stands keng-ch'en.

literal: Keng-shen is probably a corruption for keng-ch'en.
idiomatic: Keng-shen is probably a scribal error for keng-ch'en.

literal: Southern Hsü, Southern Yu, and the region west of the Che River in Yang Province. All editions agree.
idiomatic: Southern Hsü, Southern Yu, and the region west of the Che River in Yang Province. All editions agree.

literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties has the two characters nan-yen after "nan-hsü."
idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties inserts nan-yen after nan-hsü.

literal: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling and Governor of Southern Yu Province, was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army. "Chun": all editions read "Tsan"; the Three Dynasties edition reads "hui."
idiomatic: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling and Governor of Southern Yu Province, was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the Army. "Chun": all editions read "Tsan"; the Three Dynasties edition reads "hui."

literal: According to the chronology, at this time it was Prince of Wu-ling Chun—later Emperor Hsiao-wu.
idiomatic: At this date the prince was Wu-ling Chun—the future Emperor Hsiao-wu.

literal: Tsan was the ninth son of Emperor Ming; he too was later enfeoffed as Prince of Wu-ling, but at this time he had not yet been born.
idiomatic: Tsan was the ninth son of Emperor Ming; he too would later be Prince of Wu-ling, but had not yet been born.

literal: Now changed to read "Chun."
idiomatic: The text is corrected to Chun.

literal: Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ching Province. "Governor of Southern Hsü Province": all editions omit the character nan; supplied according to the biography of Yixuan.
idiomatic: Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ching Province. "Governor of Southern Hsü Province": all editions omit nan; restored from the biography of Yixuan.

literal: In the ninth month, chi-wei. "Chi-wei": all editions read "i-wei"; the Bureau edition reads "chi-wei."
idiomatic: Ninth month, chi-wei. "Chi-wei": all editions read i-wei; the Bureau edition reads chi-wei.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-ssu; the third day was chi-wei—there was no i-wei.
idiomatic: That month's new moon was ting-ssu; the third day was chi-wei—there was no i-wei.

literal: Now follow the Bureau edition.
idiomatic: The Bureau reading is adopted.
